column2: Celebrate Pokrov
Beseech Holy Protection through Her intercessions...

In the olden days, the apparition of the Theotokos ascended to Earth in Tsargrad, where she knelt and prayed with tears for the protection of all the faithful in the world. The heavenly patroness has extended her cloak over the hosts, and we will appeal to Pokrov on her feast day.
Our Lady...
The holiday begins with an all-night vigil, where many nobles and commoners have gathered together in preparation for the Great Feast.
Sub tuum praesidium.
Let the feast begin!
Pokrov

At the beginning of the feast, the icon of the Theotokos is brought and paraded before the people, then the feast begins. All come together for the coming day of feasting, where everyone gathers to eat good food and appreciate the protection of the Theotokos. Songs are sung and much merriment is had, with stories of the Cossacks of old being exchanged by the old men. The feast day ends with everyone lumbering back home, full and comfortable feeling the protection of the Theotokos.
Until next year.
Choose your svyatiye

Svyatiye Geórgios, Svyatiye Demetrios and Svyatiye Ioann are the greatest intercessors of the Gospodar, after Venerable Jesus Nazariy and the Theotokos. As a believer in the Gospodar, you can choose which of them you will honor more particularly and more than your other brothers in faith.

May Svyatiye Geórgios teach me how to fight
May Svyatiye Demetrios teach me how to govern what is mine
May Svyatiye Ioann teach me humility of spirit and unwavering faith
Go on a pilgrimage

For the warriors loyal to the Gospodar, a pilgrimage to holy cities, icons, and sanctuaries is one of the greatest ways to pay homage to Him as their Hetman. As one who believes in the Gospodar and His Celestial Host, you too may embark on this journey for the Gospodar’s glory, earning merit within the ranks of the Celestial Host’s warriors as well as earthly renown.
Pilgrimage Destination

Any worshiper of Gospodar who wishes to emulate their devout ancestors may undertake a pilgrimage to one of the holy sites of the Cossack faith: Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia, or Constantinople. These three cities hold great significance for your faith. Kyiv, long a center of Ukrainian monasticism and divine worship. Constantinople, where, according to tradition, the Theotokos appeared and knelt in tearful prayer for the protection of all the faithful, inspiring the Feast of the Pokrov, celebrated by all Cossacks. There is also Zaporizhzhia, the traditional seat of the Cossack Hetmans, home to figures such as Khmelnytsky, Yurko Bohun, and Hetman Skoropadsky. The choice of where to go and where to pay homage to the Gospodar is yours.
Go to Kyiv, the spiritual capital of all cossacks
Go to Tsargrad, the city of Theotokos
Go to Zaporizhzhia, the capital of Hetmans
Call off your pilgrimage
Departure

You set out for Kyiv,the spiritual heart of Ruthenia and the seat of the Hetmans during the Hetmanate’s greatest glory. The Batiushka blesses you for the journey and prays to the Lord for graces to be bestowed upon you, and for the strengthening of your courage, honor, and perseverance. Meanwhile, you embark on this journey alone, praying for a safe passage and the attainment of new earthly and spiritual blessings.

You set out for Tsargrad, where, as the priests of your faith teach, the Theotokos once descended to earth, knelt, and prayed with tears for the protection of all the faithful across the world. Batiushka blesses you for the journey and prays to the Gospodar for graces to be bestowed upon you, and for the strengthening of your courage, honor, and perseverance. Meanwhile, you embark on this journey alone, praying for a safe passage and the attainment of new earthly and spiritual graces.

You set out for Zaporizhzhia, where, centuries ago, all the Hetmans anointed by the Gospodar held sway. The Batiushka blesses you for the journey and prays to the Gospodar for graces to be bestowed upon you, for the strengthening of your courage, honor, and perseverance. Meanwhile, you embark on this journey alone, praying for a safe passage and the attainment of new earthly and spiritual graces.
Saints, protect me!
End of the Pilgrimage

You arrive in Zaporizhzhia, the former seat of all the Hetmans who served the Gospodar. It was here that Hetman Sahaidachny founded the Sich, and here that the martyr Ivan Skoropadsky was elected the new Hetman, a man who, by a special privilege granted by the Gospodar at the Arkhistrateg’s intercession, lived for five hundred years until he was slain by the godless, freedom-hating Hungarians. You stroll through the streets of Zaporizhzhia, picturing the Cossack assemblies of old and the heroes of the faith as they delivered their speeches. You reach the Cathedral dedicated to the Theotokos and step inside. You are greeted by the sight of beautiful frescoes, and at the far end, you see the iconostasis barring the way between the fleeting glory of earthly warriors and the true glory of the Gospodar. You kneel to thank Gospodar for the grace of having arrived here, and you ask his saints, to intercede with your Supreme Hetman on your behalf, seeking the grace of glory both on Earth and in Heaven.

You have finally arrived at Constantinople, a city forever imbued with the spirit of what Iisus Nazariy represents. Before you rises an immense and ancient metropolis whose towering walls, crowded harbors, and countless domes dwarf every city you have seen on your pilgrimage. As you make your way through the winding streets in search of lodging, your senses are overwhelmed by the cries of merchants, the mingling scents of incense and spice, and the endless throngs of travelers and sailors from far and wide. You wander these old streets until you reach the Patriarchal Cathedral of St. George, built in honor of the saint known among your fellow believers as Svyatiye Geórgios. Stepping inside and beholding the cathedral's majesty, you kneel near the iconostasis and offer prayers to the Gospodar through the intercession of Svyatiye Geórgios, giving thanks for your safe arrival and asking for the grace of glory on Earth and in Heaven.

You arrive in Kyiv, the first capital of Ruthenia, the spiritual center of the faith of the warrior-god Gospodar and the cult of the Theotokos—a place where, according to tradition, great hetmans at the height of the Sich’s glory once held sway and governed Ruthenia in defiance of the Latins, the Russians, and the Turks. You pass many churches in the city before reaching the most important among them: Saint Sophia's Cathedral. Legend holds that it existed even before Gospodar became the principal deity of Ruthenia, making it the oldest church in this part of the world. Stepping inside, you gaze upon beautiful mosaics and frescoes depicting saints, marveling at their splendor as you make your way to the chancel and the altar, which is screened by an iconostasis. You pause to offer silent prayers to Gospodar and his saints, giving thanks for the grace of having reached this place and asking for the grace of glory on Earth and in Heaven.
Glory to Gospodar!

St. George's Cathedral in Constantinople, dedicated to Saint George, known to you as Svyatiye Geórgios, invites you to reflect on adopting Svyatiye Geórgios as your patron saint and an object of your special devotion.
Take Svyatiye Geórgios as your patron
Another saint is already your patron, remain faithful to him
Do not take on a patron
Kyiv is a regional hub not only for spiritual culture but also for scholarship. Upon leaving the cathedral, you hear about numerous opportunities to deepen your religious or tactical knowledge.
Spend time learning tactics from a local military instructor
Spend time receiving religious instruction from a local monk
Spend time intensively learning about types of alcohol at a local tavern

As you walk through Zaporizhzhia, you hear not only about your own faith but also encounter people who believe in Gospodar differently than you do, yet similarly, though differing significantly in the details.
Maybe they are right...
So?
Heretics!
As you wander through the wild fields, you suddenly see bandits walking towards you with swords in their hands...
Arkhistrateg, pray for me...

As you travel, you encounter other riders of your faith. They greet you warmly, and as you talk, they tell you that merchants have set up nearby with their wares—and that they need people like you to seize what is "theirs."
Why not?
Politely decline

Attacking the merchants turns out to be your greatest mistake. Unfortunately for you, the local lord was patrolling the area and quickly routed the band you were part of. To your further misfortune, he is a man of principle
column3: he cares nothing for your standing among your own kind—only that you have committed a crime and must face punishment...

Pay the ransom

Nice

Monastery

On your journey, you come across a monastery—an ancient one teeming with monks. The sight of it fills you with a sense of peace and bliss. As you draw closer, some monks returning with herbs stop to speak with you, telling you of the power of herbs to heal the troubled mind and conquer even the most stubborn of ailments.
Stay at the monastery for a few days as a guest
Go further

After a few days, you leave the monastery. Yet, someone remains to remind you of your stay, for during that time you befriended one of the talented monks who, with the superior's permission, left the monastery to assist in your spiritual growth and tend to your healing whenever necessary.
Nice
After a few days, you leave the monastery. The time spent there has soothed your nerves. You feel more relaxed than ever before.
After a few days, you leave the monastery. Your time there allowed you to devote more of yourself to prayer to Gospodar, free from other distractions.
